description: Shape-based handwriting recognition geometry rules. Each character has properties to check against drawn input.

boundingBox.description: Nearly square or slightly wider than tall

curves.description: One main loop forming the character

strokes.description: Can be drawn as 1 continuous stroke or multiple strokes forming the shape

geometryRules.description: Roughly circular shape with opening at bottom-right

tolerance.description: Allow up to 15% deviation from ideal shape

curves.description: One main loop with an additional vertical element

geometryRules.description: Similar to അ but with a vertical mark or extension

strokes.description: Complex shape with multiple connected strokes

geometryRules.description: Angular character with a curved top-left and pointed right side

tolerance.description: Allow up to 20% deviation due to complexity

bumps.description: Characteristic bumps or waves in the shape

geometryRules.description: Wide character with multiple peaks across the top and a baseline

strokes.description: Base character strokes plus diacritic mark strokes

geometryRules.description: ക with a diacritic mark (ാ) added below or to the right

tolerance.description: Allow up to 25% deviation due to compound complexity

boundingBox.description: Wider than tall or roughly square

strokes.description: Base character strokes plus diacritic mark

steps.name: Stroke Normalization
steps.description: Resample drawn stroke(s) to a fixed number of points. Remove noise. Calculate bounding box.

steps.name: Feature Extraction
steps.description: Measure aspect ratio, detect loops, count curves, identify key points (corners, endpoints)

steps.name: Geometry Matching
steps.description: Check if extracted features match target character's geometry rules within tolerance

steps.name: Classification
steps.description: Return: Correct (>90% match), Understandable (70-90% match), or Incorrect (<70% match)

factors: Handwriting variation is natural — allow for individual style
Size variation is allowed — aspect ratio matters more than absolute size
Stroke order doesn't matter — only final shape is evaluated
Slight distortions and imprecisions are acceptable
